claims.text: Two calls in one day asked how to copy the owner's email setup, so the article is the walkthrough.
claims.quote: Two calls in one day asked the same thing, how do I copy your email setup, so this is the walkthrough.

claims.text: It is the first agentic email workflow the owner has run that puts him more in control, and the reason is the behaviour policies, not the model.
claims.quote: puts me more in control rather than less, and the reason is the behaviour policies, not the model.

claims.text: Claude as an agent state machine: each role is a Claude session that reads its state from a vault, does one kind of work, and writes the result back as files.
claims.quote: Each role is a Claude session that reads its state from a vault, does one kind of work, and writes the result back as files.

claims.text: The agent gets a Google Workspace mailbox of its own on a domain you own; your own inbox is never connected.
claims.quote: The agent gets a Google Workspace mailbox of its own, on a domain you own.

claims.text: On a Team plan the connectors are enabled by the organisation owner and connected from the agent's own account, so the OAuth grants to Gmail, Calendar and Drive are held by that account alone.
claims.quote: the OAuth grants to Gmail, Calendar and Drive are held by that account and no other.

claims.text: The inbox agent's behaviour policy is written before the first run, even when there is only one agent.
claims.quote: Before the first run, write its behaviour policy, and write it even though there is only one agent.

claims.text: On a Team plan most barriers are the policy and nothing technical: the same scope that lets the agent draft lets it send, and the one that lets it read lets it delete.
claims.quote: the same scope that lets the agent draft lets it send, and the same scope that lets it read lets it delete.

claims.text: Every role's account has the same reach to the mailbox; two have it in their mandate, and only one may write.
claims.quote: Every one of these accounts has the same reach to the mailbox. Two have it in their mandate, and only one may write.

claims.text: Email-FS lite: each agent has an inbox, which is a folder, and a message is a file with a sender, a recipient, a subject and a body with typed blocks.
claims.quote: each agent has an inbox, which is a folder, and a message is a file with a sender, a recipient, a subject and a body

claims.text: Each role writes only its own folders, and a cycle is one commit, made after a leak check that refuses any file containing a key shape.
claims.quote: a cycle is one commit, after a leak check that refuses any file containing a key shape.

claims.text: Four scheduled runs a day committing once per role is about fifty commits a day; after three days the collaboration vault took seven minutes to clone and two sessions timed out.
claims.quote: after three days the collaboration vault took seven minutes to clone, and two sessions timed out on it.

value.unit: minutes to clone the collaboration vault after three days

claims.text: Commit once per run rather than once per role, and compact when a clone passes five minutes by seeding a fresh vault from the current files and freezing the old one.
claims.quote: compact when a clone passes five minutes, which means seeding a fresh vault from the current files and freezing the old one as the archive.

claims.text: Every interface the team built was made by an agent in an afternoon because the data was already files in a vault, and each interface got a policy of its own.
claims.quote: every one of those interfaces was built by an agent in an afternoon because the data was already files in a vault

claims.text: Because every message, draft and decision is a file or a row, the workflow leaves a footprint that can be read afterwards instead of believed.
claims.quote: You do not have to believe what the agent says it did. You can read what it did.

claims.text: A conductor session runs each role exactly once in a fixed order, each as a sub-agent with a twelve-minute time box, leak-checking and pushing after every step.
claims.quote: runs each role exactly once in a fixed order, each as a sub-agent with a twelve-minute time box

claims.text: A security role runs first, checking for drift, keys in files and unintroduced identities, and last, checking what the run changed and whether it was allowed.
claims.quote: A security role runs first (did anything drift since last time, is there a key in a file, is there an identity nobody introduced) and last

claims.text: Nothing is sent by an agent: the drafts role puts replies in Drafts and the person reads, edits and presses send.
claims.quote: Nothing is sent by an agent. The drafts role puts replies in Drafts.

claims.text: The one exception is a security finding: the security role may send one email, to one address, with one subject prefix, only when it has found something critical.
claims.quote: The security role may send one email, to one address (the person's own), with one subject prefix, and only when it has found something critical

claims.text: A security hold stops the conductor, every role and every page until the person releases it with a note; the security role cannot lift its own.
claims.quote: Only the person releases the hold, with a note of what was done. The security role cannot lift its own.

claims.text: On day five a vault key was found quoted inside a session capture an agent had committed, and redacting the file would have left the key in the history.
claims.quote: on day five a vault key was found quoted inside a session capture an agent had committed.

claims.text: A leaked write key means a new vault, not an edit, and the pre-commit scan looks for other people's secret shapes as well as your own.
claims.quote: a leaked write key means a new vault, not an edit

claims.text: The dev agent shipped nineteen releases of the collaboration UI in eight days and wrote the first policy for five roles that did not yet exist.
claims.quote: In eight days I shipped nineteen releases of the collaboration UI

value.unit: releases of the collaboration UI in eight days

claims.text: The roster as drawn by the briefs role on 2 October is twelve agents, not the five of phase 2.
claims.quote: The roster is twelve agents, not the five of phase 2

claims.text: The briefs role's card corrects the schedule: the conductor runs four times a day on weekdays and twice at weekends, in the order security, drafts, inbox, briefs, CRM, webSummit, abp, dev, security.
claims.quote: the conductor runs four times a day on weekdays and twice at weekends, in the order security, drafts, inbox, briefs, CRM, webSummit, abp, dev, security.

claims.text: The @zapier role relays WhatsApp through Zapier and Twilio; its policy is written and the channel is not yet live.
claims.quote: @zapier (WhatsApp relay through Zapier and Twilio, with its policy written and the channel not yet live)

claims.text: Trust is built from a record of drafts the owner did not have to change, and the record is there to read.
claims.quote: Trust is built from a record of drafts I did not have to change, and the record is there to read.

claims.text: When an agent is one day allowed to send, it will be one agent, one kind of message, with a policy row that says so, and the footprint will show whether it was right.
claims.quote: it will be one agent, one kind of message, with a policy row that says so

claims.text: The article is the how, in phases; it is not the argument for why, which is in the earlier articles.
claims.quote: It is not the argument for why

claims.text: The eight figures are mock-ups and infographics with fictional names, addresses, paths and numbers, and no live data.
claims.quote: the figures are mock-ups and infographics with fictional names, addresses, paths and numbers

claims.text: Only the dev agent's account of its role has arrived; the other agents' accounts are to follow.
claims.quote: The other agents' accounts of their roles are to follow.

claims.text: The agent's GitHub account is created with the agent's Google account, so there is one identity to manage.
claims.quote: Sign up with the agent's Google account, so there is one identity to manage

claims.text: The append-lane messaging and Agent Contact write-ups on sgit.ai give the file shapes the agents talk in.
claims.quote: Agent Contact is the same idea between sites.
